# wso2is_identity_provider (Resource)

Manages an identity provider, which the Console calls a connection. An identity provider lets users sign in with another system. Examples are social logins (Google, GitHub, Facebook, Microsoft and Apple) and any OpenID Connect or SAML provider. The resource also manages claim and role mappings, just-in-time provisioning and outbound provisioning.

Authenticator and connector settings are properties with the names that the server uses. The `wso2is_federated_authenticator_metadata` data source lists them. The provider only manages the property keys that you set. Put secrets in `secret_properties`, so that plans hide them. To use the identity provider for login, add it to an application's `authentication_sequence`. To import, use the identity provider's ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "wso2is_identity_provider" "google" {
  name        = "Google"
  template_id = "google-idp"
  federated_authenticators = {
    GoogleOIDCAuthenticator = {
      properties = {
        ClientId    = "1234.apps.googleusercontent.com"
        callbackUrl = "https://id.example.com/commonauth"
      }
      secret_properties = {
        ClientSecret = var.google_client_secret
      }
    }
  }
  jit_provisioning = {
    enabled = true
    scheme  = "PROVISION_SILENTLY"
  }
}

resource "wso2is_identity_provider" "corporate" {
  name     = "Corporate SSO"
  jwks_uri = "https://sso.corp.example/jwks"
  federated_authenticators = {
    OpenIDConnectAuthenticator = {
      properties = {
        ClientId         = "wso2is"
        OAuth2AuthzEPUrl = "https://sso.corp.example/authorize"
        OAuth2TokenEPUrl = "https://sso.corp.example/token"
        UserInfoUrl      = "https://sso.corp.example/userinfo"
        callbackUrl      = "https://id.example.com/commonauth"
        Scopes           = "openid email profile"
      }
      secret_properties = {
        ClientSecret = var.corporate_client_secret
      }
    }
  }
  claims = {
    user_id_claim = "email"
    mappings = [
      { idp_claim = "email", local_claim = "http://wso2.org/claims/emailaddress" },
    ]
  }
  role_mappings = [
    { idp_role = "admins", local_role = "Internal/admin" },
  ]
}

variable "google_client_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "corporate_client_secret" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Unique name, used in authentication steps.

### Optional

- `alias` (String) Alias used as the audience of tokens this provider issues (for example the token endpoint of the resident IdP).
- `certificates` (List of String) PEM certificates of the provider (for validating signed responses and tokens). Conflicts with `jwks_uri`.
- `claims` (Attributes) Claim mappings from the provider's attributes to local claims. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--claims))
- `default_authenticator` (String) Name of the federated authenticator used by default. The default is the only (or first) configured authenticator.
- `default_outbound_connector` (String) Name of the default outbound provisioning connector.
- `description` (String) Description.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the connection can be used. The default is `true`.
- `federated_authenticators` (Attributes Map) Federated authenticators, keyed by authenticator name: `GoogleOIDCAuthenticator`, `GithubAuthenticator`, `FacebookAuthenticator`, `MicrosoftWindowsLiveAuthenticator`, `Office365Authenticator`, `AppleOIDCAuthenticator`, `TwitterAuthenticator`, `OpenIDConnectAuthenticator`, `SAMLSSOAuthenticator`, `PassiveSTSAuthenticator`, `IWAKerberosAuthenticator`, `EmailOTP`, `SMSOTP`, or a custom authenticator. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--federated_authenticators))
- `force_delete` (Boolean) Delete the connection even when applications still use it. The default is `false`.
- `groups` (Set of String) Groups defined at the provider that can be mapped to local roles.
- `home_realm_identifier` (String) Home realm identifier (`fidp` request parameter value) that selects this provider.
- `idp_issuer_name` (String) Issuer of tokens from this provider, when different from its name (used to validate JWT bearer grants).
- `image_url` (String) Logo URL.
- `implicit_association` (Attributes) Associate federated users with local users that have matching attributes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--implicit_association))
- `is_federation_hub` (Boolean) The provider is a federation hub (it fronts other providers). The default is `false`.
- `is_primary` (Boolean) Use as the primary (default) identity provider. The default is `false`.
- `jit_provisioning` (Attributes) Just-in-time provisioning of local accounts for federated users. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--jit_provisioning))
- `jwks_uri` (String) JWKS endpoint used to validate tokens signed by the provider. Conflicts with `certificates`.
- `outbound_provisioning_connectors` (Attributes Map) Outbound provisioning connectors keyed by name: `SCIM2`, `scim`, `googleapps`, `salesforce`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--outbound_provisioning_connectors))
- `outbound_provisioning_roles` (Set of String) Only users with these roles are provisioned to this provider.
- `role_mappings` (Attributes Set) Provider role to local role mappings. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--role_mappings))
- `template_id` (String) The Console template, for example `google-idp`, `github-idp`, `enterprise-oidc-idp` or `enterprise-saml-idp`. The template only changes how the Console shows the connection. The server only accepts it at creation, so changing it replaces the connection.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identity provider ID.

<a id="nestedatt--claims"></a>
### Nested Schema for `claims`

Optional:

- `mappings` (Attributes Set) Provider claim to local claim mappings. Without mappings the provider's claims are used as is. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--claims--mappings))
- `provisioning_claims` (Attributes Set) Default values of claims for outbound provisioning. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--claims--provisioning_claims))
- `role_claim` (String) Provider claim that carries roles.
- `user_id_claim` (String) The identity provider's claim that identifies the user. When it is empty, the server uses the subject.

<a id="nestedatt--claims--mappings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `claims.mappings`

Required:

- `idp_claim` (String) Claim name used by the provider.
- `local_claim` (String) Local claim URI.


<a id="nestedatt--claims--provisioning_claims"></a>
### Nested Schema for `claims.provisioning_claims`

Required:

- `claim` (String) Claim URI.
- `default_value` (String) Default value.



<a id="nestedatt--federated_authenticators"></a>
### Nested Schema for `federated_authenticators`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the authenticator is enabled. The default is `true`.
- `endpoint` (Attributes) External service endpoint of a custom (user defined) federated authenticator. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--federated_authenticators--endpoint))
- `properties` (Map of String) Authenticator properties, for example `ClientId`, `callbackUrl`, `Scopes`, `OAuth2AuthzEPUrl`, `OAuth2TokenEPUrl`, `UserInfoUrl` (OIDC) or `IdPEntityId`, `SSOUrl`, `SPEntityId` (SAML).
- `secret_properties` (Map of String, Sensitive) Confidential properties, for example `ClientSecret`.

<a id="nestedatt--federated_authenticators--endpoint"></a>
### Nested Schema for `federated_authenticators.endpoint`

Required:

- `authentication_type` (String) `NONE`, `BASIC`, `BEARER` or `API_KEY`.
- `uri` (String) HTTPS endpoint.

Optional:

- `authentication_properties` (Map of String, Sensitive) Credentials: `username`/`password` (BASIC), `accessToken` (BEARER) or `header`/`value` (API_KEY). The server never returns this value.



<a id="nestedatt--implicit_association"></a>
### Nested Schema for `implicit_association`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable implicit association. The default is `false`.
- `lookup_attributes` (List of String) Local claim URIs used to find the local user.


<a id="nestedatt--jit_provisioning"></a>
### Nested Schema for `jit_provisioning`

Optional:

- `account_lookup_attribute_mappings` (Attributes List) Local and federated attributes used to find an existing local user. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--jit_provisioning--account_lookup_attribute_mappings))
- `associate_local_user` (Boolean) Link to an existing local user found through the lookup attributes. The default is `false`.
- `attribute_sync_method` (String) `OVERRIDE_ALL`, `PRESERVE_LOCAL` or `NONE`. The default is `OVERRIDE_ALL`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Create local users on first login. The default is `false`.
- `idp_group_sync_method` (String) `MERGE_WITH_EXISTING` or `OVERRIDE_ALL`. The default is `MERGE_WITH_EXISTING`.
- `scheme` (String) `PROVISION_SILENTLY`, `PROMPT_CONSENT`, `PROMPT_PASSWORD_CONSENT` or `PROMPT_USERNAME_PASSWORD_CONSENT`. The default is `PROVISION_SILENTLY`.
- `skip_jit_for_lookup_failure` (Boolean) Skip provisioning when the local user lookup fails. The default is `false`.
- `user_store` (String) User store for provisioned users. The default is `PRIMARY`.

<a id="nestedatt--jit_provisioning--account_lookup_attribute_mappings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `jit_provisioning.account_lookup_attribute_mappings`

Required:

- `federated_attribute` (String) Provider claim.
- `local_attribute` (String) Local claim URI.



<a id="nestedatt--outbound_provisioning_connectors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `outbound_provisioning_connectors`

Optional:

- `blocking_enabled` (Boolean) Provision synchronously.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Enabled. The default is `true`.
- `properties` (Map of String) Connector properties, for example `scim2-user-ep`, `scim2-username`.
- `rules_enabled` (Boolean) Apply provisioning rules.
- `secret_properties` (Map of String, Sensitive) Confidential connector properties, for example `scim2-password`.


<a id="nestedatt--role_mappings"></a>
### Nested Schema for `role_mappings`

Required:

- `idp_role` (String) Role name sent by the provider.
- `local_role` (String) Local role, as `Internal/<role name>` for organization roles (WSO2 silently ignores other formats).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import wso2is_identity_provider.google <identity_provider_id>
```
